claim: coordinator._command_valve_target (smart_write) writes the degC valve target with no unit conversion
v1_number: no finder harness (lead never measured); l1 arms: climate on degF instance written=21.0 expected=69.8 abs_err=48.8; number declaring degF written=21.0 expected=69.8 abs_err=48.8
v2_number: sibling arbiter path at main (pump_arbiter._write, climate slot, degF instance): written=21.0 expected=69.8 abs_err=48.8; setpoint_check._setpoint_and_unit reads climate in hass units, so read and write disagree
v2_metric: abs error between the service value and the target in the unit HA interprets it in (climate: hass.config.units.temperature_unit per climate/__init__.py 2026.9.3 L826-830; number: declared unit)
null_control: climate on degC instance abs_err=0.0; number declaring degC abs_err=0.0
perturbation: one line before the write: target=temperature_from_c(target, hass unit for climate / declared unit for number) -> both arms 48.8 -> 0.0, nulls stay 0.0
attacks: reach: config_flow offers number/input_number/climate for CONF_MIXING_VALVE_WRITE_ENTITY (config_flow.py:1689); real HA climate converts the service value FROM the instance unit and range-checks it (ServiceValidationError temp_out_of_range) -> on a degF instance 21 (indoor) or 35-45 (flow kind) is read as degF: refused when below min_temp, else the device is set ~-6 degC / 2-7 degC; a number with device_class temperature declares the instance unit, so every degF install is affected; degC instances (the null) unaffected
class: bug, unit conversion at a device write (N-unit family)
notes: arch3-s6 does NOT fix it: its coordinator hunk routes the valve through inputs.write_setpoint (value 'already in the entity's own unit', no conversion), while the same diff adds write_setpoint_c (converting) and uses it only for the arbiter. Fix = call write_setpoint_c in _command_valve_target. arch3-s6 does fix the sibling arbiter climate write (pump_arbiter._write -> write_setpoint_c).

attacks: reach: restore_session is spawned in the coordinator constructor (coordinator.py ~2647); the window is the startup store-load (an executor file read, behind ~13 sibling loads spawned in the same loop); A/B need a user or automation away/boost write inside that window (no RestoreEntity or startup writer of these exists: grep switch.py/services.py); C needs the first full solve's _resolve_away (coordinator.py:5693) before the load completes, and that solve follows the light first refresh plus price and weather fetches -- a narrow window not measured here; consequence is a lost away/boost toggle, no unsafe write
